Got it—let’s add Google Analytics (GA) to your Next.js site on Vercel.  
We’ll:
1. Grab your GA Tracking ID (the one that starts with **G‑** or **UA‑**).  
2. Save it in Vercel’s environment variables so it never leaks.  
3. Add the GA script in `app/layout.tsx` (or `pages/_app.tsx`) so it loads on every page.  
4. Verify the script is on the page and that GA sees a hit.

---

### Quick safety check

| Step | Why it’s safe |
|------|---------------|
| **Use a Vercel env var** – not hard‑coded | Keeps the ID secret, even in the repo |
| **Add the script in the `<Head>`** – not inline in user code | Keeps the rest of your app untouched |
| **No “magic” rights** – no new data storage or logins | Keeps your danger level low |

---

### 1️⃣  Prepare a save point

If you’re on a Git repo, just commit now (e.g. `git commit -m "save - ready for GA"`).  
If not, fork the folder or make a quick copy to your computer.

---

### 2️⃣  Store the tracking ID in Vercel

1. **Get the ID**  
   • If you already created a GA property, copy the ID that looks like `G‑XXXXXXX` or `UA‑XXXXX‑X`.  
   • If you haven’t, create a free GA account first.  
2. **Add to Vercel**  
   • Go to **Vercel > Projects > Your project > Settings > Environment Variables**.  
   • Click **Add**.  
   • Variable name: `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID`  
   • Value: *your tracking ID*  
   • Environment: **Production** (and optionally **Preview** if you want tracking on preview URLs).  
   • Click **Save**.

> **Note**: The `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix makes the value available on the client side, but it’s still kept out of the repo.

---

### 3️⃣  Insert the GA script in your Next.js app

#### If you’re using the new app router (`app/` folder)

Add this to `app/layout.tsx` (or any file that renders on every route):

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import Script from 'next/script';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const gaId = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID!; // non‑null assertion: we know it exists
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* Existing head content */}
        <Script
          strategy="afterInteractive"
          dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
            __html: `
              window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
              function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
              gtag('js', new Date());
              gtag('config', '${gaId}');
            `,
          }}
        />
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

> `strategy="afterInteractive"` loads the script once the page is ready, keeping performance optimal.

#### If you’re using the old pages router (`pages/` folder)

Edit `pages/_app.tsx`:

```tsx
import Script from 'next/script';

function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) {
  const gaId = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID!;

  return (
    <>
      <Script
        strategy="afterInteractive"
        dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
          __html: `
            window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
            function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
            gtag('js', new Date());
            gtag('config', '${gaId}');
          `,
        }}
      />
      <Component {...pageProps} />
    </>
  );
}

export default MyApp;
```

---

### 4️⃣  Deploy

Push your changes to Vercel (GitHub, GitLab, or Vercel’s UI).  
Vercel will pick up the new env var and rebuild.

---

### 5️⃣  Verify GA is working

1. Open your site in a browser.  
2. Open DevTools ➜ **Console**.  
   You should see no errors and a line similar to:

   ```
   gtag is not defined
   ```

   (If you see this, double‑check the `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` variable.)

3. In GA’s Real‑Time > Overview, you should see a “0 – 1” hit when you refresh the page.

---

### 6️⃣  Wrap up safety

- **Commit** the updated `env` config and layout file.  
- **Do NOT** add the GA ID directly to any file that ends up in the repo.  
- **Keep** the GA ID in Vercel so that if you ever re‑clone the repo, you won’t need to re‑enter it.

---

Let me know if you need help creating the GA account, or if you see any errors when you test. Happy tracking!
